about: Claims of the public page and where each number comes from on the internal page. Read by build_public.py, which checks every entry
and writes public_evidence_manifest.json (development only, never shipped), and by check_public.py (rules T01 to T03).
claims[]: id, section, public_claim (the sentence as shown on the page, word for word), datasets, figure_asset (a public figure id pub_...,
a file under site/ such as assets/img/compact_state.webp, a list of those, or null), numbers[], and optionally shown[], support[], evidence_note.
shown[]: exact strings of the page that carry numbers of the claim outside its sentence (stat tiles such as 'TACO 0.85 119 events').
The claim sentence and every shown string must be on the page word for word, each inside one text block; a number of the page text is accepted
only inside such a string of a claim that lists it (or inside a structural phrase), so a number moved to another sentence or dataset stops the build.
numbers[]: displayed (the number as shown: '37.1', '46%', '0.85'), dataset, metric, full_value (the full-precision internal value),
transform (optional; how displayed derives from full_value: identity | percent | abs | abs_percent | one_minus_percent |
minus_one_percent), internal_block (block id of docs/evidence_manifest.json), internal_evidence, internal_report, source_file,
locator (optional; filled from the internal evidence when left out), where (optional: 'chart' for a number that the page shows only as a value
label of the public chart named in figure_asset; the build then checks that the chart plots that value for that dataset), note (optional, for readers).
support[]: values that back a claim shown without a digit ('unchanged', 'no reduction', 'almost only'). Same fields as a number, with shown_as (the words
of the page they back) instead of displayed; checked against the internal evidence like a number, never counted as a number of the page.
A supporting value marked where: 'chart' backs a number that is TYPED into a label of a public chart (the number of events of a kind in an
axis label): shown_as is then that label, word for word. The build checks that the label is written in the panel of that dataset of a chart
named in figure_asset and that it holds the value; a number typed into an axis label without such an entry stops the build.
A claim needs at least one of numbers, support or evidence_note (free text for readers; not machine-checked).
internal_evidence is one of: {evidence_file: 'docs/evidence/<unit>.json', key: '<label of the number>', value_index: n (which number of
the stored value, 0 = first; needed when it holds several), entry: i (optional)} | {figure: '<internal figure id>', panel, series,
category, bound: 'lo' | 'hi' (optional)} or {figure, panel, ref: '<reference line label>'} | {json_file: 'docs/...json', path: [...], value_index: n}.
structural_numbers[]: numbers of the page text that are not measurements (sizes, counts, names, dates, thresholds). Each entry is a
phrase ('text', matched without regard to case) or a 'regex', with the reason ('why').
chart_text_numbers{}: per public figure, the numbers written in its title, labels and note in the chart data file (sample sizes, sizes of the
descriptions, counts). A number of those strings that is not listed here (and is not structural) stops the build, and so does a listed number that is
no longer written. The build also requires every digit run of those strings to occur in the strings of the internal figure the chart is derived from.

The second sentence of the paragraph ('We read this as contact dynamics depending on the interaction regime (the test sets also differ in composition), not as a failure of either dataset.') is a reading, not a tested cause: the test sets also differ in size and composition.
